subdomains.business_boundary: Professional aerospace and mechanical engineering analysis and design services spanning spacecraft thermal control, structural integrity, and mechanical system verification.
subdomains.occupations: Aerospace thermal engineer; Mechanical/structural analyst; Propulsion and mechanisms engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Excludes low-thrust orbit transfer (already an official task); expands into thermal, structural FEA, and mechanical design verification workflows.

subdomains.business_boundary: Electronic design, verification, and test engineering services covering high-speed PCB signal integrity, IC design-for-testability, and power conversion.
subdomains.occupations: Signal integrity engineer; DFT/test engineer; Power electronics engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Boundary is the electronic design/verification service, not KiCad/LTspice tool operation.

subdomains.business_boundary: Civil, structural, and geospatial engineering services covering survey/LiDAR data production, hydraulic modeling, and structural analysis.
subdomains.occupations: Geospatial/LiDAR engineer; Hydraulic and hydrology engineer; Structural engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Excludes CAD/BIM from 2D drawings, highway alignment, and geotech excavation (already official); adds LiDAR, hydraulics, and structural analysis.

subdomains.business_boundary: Chemical and process engineering services covering steady-state process simulation, process safety analysis, and process design documentation.
subdomains.occupations: Process engineer; Process safety engineer; P&ID/process drafter
subdomains.boundary_note: uncovered_official — no official ALE task exists for this subdomain; all workflows sourced from industry material (E3) or marked E4.

subdomains.business_boundary: Manufacturing and industrial systems quality/process engineering services covering dimensional inspection, statistical process control, and tolerance analysis.
subdomains.occupations: Quality engineer; Metrology engineer; Manufacturing/process engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Excludes CAM toolpath-only work (already official); expands into inspection, SPC, and tolerance/quality workflows.

candidates.workflow_title: Spacecraft thermal control subsystem sizing (radiator and heater design)
candidates.workflow_summary: Compute component heat dissipation, build a thermal node network, size radiators for worst-hot case and heaters for worst-cold case, and verify temperature margins against requirements.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Component power dissipation table, thermal requirements (temperature limits), material thermal properties, orbit/environment definition, radiator area constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: NASA public technical reports; an expert supplies the dissipation and requirement data as task input.
candidates.task_input: A defined spacecraft/equipment box with component power map, allowed temperature range, and orbital thermal environment.
candidates.professional_operations: Enumerate heat loads for hot and cold cases, build thermal node/network model, compute radiative and conductive paths, size radiator area and heater power, iterate to meet margins.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Thermal control design report with node temperatures, radiator and heater sizing, and margin table vs requirements.
candidates.success_criteria: All node temperatures stay within limits with positive margin across hot and cold cases; radiator/heater sizing is physically consistent.
candidates.verification_approach: Check against a reference thermal solver (e.g., a Python lumped-parameter model) using known Q_gen and radiator area to confirm steady-state temperatures and margin sign.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux; Python/NumPy; optionally SINDA/FLUINT or Thermal Desktop (proprietary); GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary thermal solvers may be unavailable; NASA PDF sources are E3 (could not be full-text read this round), so numbers need expert confirmation.
candidates.expert_capability: Orbital thermal analysis, radiative/conduction heat transfer, and spacecraft requirement margins.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Touches electronics (component power dissipation) but is fundamentally a thermal-control engineering task.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete end-to-end sizing workflow, not a single heat-load calculation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 only — confirm radiator-sizing method and node-model granularity with a domain expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Structural finite element analysis and margin-of-safety review of an aerospace component
candidates.workflow_summary: Build a finite element model of a load-bearing aerospace part, apply load cases, extract stress and deflection, and compute margin of safety against material allowables.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: CAD geometry, material allowables (yield/ultimate, fatigue), load cases and boundary conditions, factors of safety.
candidates.usage_permissions: Industry FEA curriculum guidance is public; expert provides geometry, loads, and allowables as task input.
candidates.task_input: A component definition with geometry, material properties, applied loads, and acceptance criteria.
candidates.professional_operations: Mesh and constrain the model, apply load cases, run static analysis, post-process stress/deflection, compute margin of safety, flag critical regions.
candidates.expected_deliverable: FEA report with mesh/load setup, stress and deflection contours, and margin-of-safety table.
candidates.success_criteria: All margins of safety positive; results converge under mesh refinement; load cases fully covered.
candidates.verification_approach: Compare peak stress and displacement against a simplified analytical hand-calc (e.g., beam/plate) within an expected tolerance band.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux; open-source FEA (e.g., CalculiX/Code_Aster) or Python; optionally Abaqus/ANSYS (proprietary).
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary solvers may be unavailable; correct boundary conditions are expertise-heavy and easy to get wrong.
candidates.expert_capability: Structural mechanics, FEA modeling, and margin-of-safety analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Touches civil_geo structural FEA but in an aerospace materials/loads context.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete modeling-to-margin workflow, not a single stress query.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 only — confirm load-case and margin convention with an aerospace structures expert.

candidates.workflow_title: Mechanical tolerance stack-up and GD&T design verification of an assembly
candidates.workflow_summary: Derive tolerance stack-ups from part-level GD&T for a multi-part assembly, compute worst-case and statistical fit/clearance, and verify assembly requirements.
candidates.source_reference: No direct source consulted; inferred from standard mechanical engineering practice.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Assembly CAD, per-part GD&T callouts, assembly functional requirements (fit/clearance), production capability data.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies proprietary assembly and tolerance data.
candidates.task_input: An assembly with part tolerances and a functional fit/clearance requirement.
candidates.professional_operations: Identify critical dimensions and datum references, build tolerance chains, compute worst-case and RSS stack-ups, compare to requirement, recommend tolerance adjustments.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Tolerance stack-up analysis report with per-chain results and a pass/fail or design-change recommendation.
candidates.success_criteria: Stack-up results correctly bound the functional requirement; datum and chain logic is traceable.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute each chain with an independent scripted worst-case/RSS calculation and match reported values.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; spreadsheet/Python; optionally a GD&T tool (proprietary).
candidates.blocking_risks: GD&T interpretation is expertise-heavy; no verified source this round so the exact convention must be expert-confirmed.
candidates.expert_capability: Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, tolerance stack-up analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps manufacturing tolerance analysis but framed as design-phase verification.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete multi-chain stack-up workflow, not a single dimension check.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E4 — requires expert confirmation of GD&T standard (ASME Y14.5) and stack-up method.

candidates.workflow_title: High-speed PCB signal integrity design and verification
candidates.workflow_summary: Route and verify a high-speed interface on a PCB with controlled impedance, differential pairs, length matching, and return-path continuity, then run pre/post-layout signal integrity checks.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Schematic with high-speed nets, layer stack-up spec, impedance targets, driver/receiver electrical characteristics.
candidates.usage_permissions: Altium documentation is public; expert provides board design and electrical specs as task input.
candidates.task_input: A high-speed interface definition with netlist, stack-up, impedance and length-match targets.
candidates.professional_operations: Set layer stack and impedance profiles, route differential pairs with clearance, apply length tuning, define return-path/stitching rules, run pre/post-layout SI analysis, adjust termination.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Completed layout with impedance/length reports and a signal-integrity verification summary.
candidates.success_criteria: Traces meet impedance (e.g., 90/100 Ohm), length-match, and clearance rules; SI simulation shows no violations.
candidates.verification_approach: Extract controlled-impedance and length values from the layout and validate against a reference rule set/DRC report.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Windows; Altium Designer (proprietary) or KiCad (open) for layout; GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Altium is proprietary and licensed; accurate stack-up data from the fabricator is required.
candidates.expert_capability: High-speed digital design, transmission-line and return-path fundamentals.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: None significant; distinct from the existing analog/KiCad tasks by high-speed SI focus.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete route-and-verify workflow, not a single via placement.

candidates.workflow_title: Design-for-testability scan chain insertion and ATPG fault coverage analysis
candidates.workflow_summary: Insert scan chains into a digital design, generate stuck-at-fault test patterns via ATPG, and compute fault coverage and defect level.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Gate-level netlist, cell library, stuck-at fault model parameters, yield estimate.
candidates.usage_permissions: ETH Zurich educational exercise is public; expert provides the design netlist and test constraints.
candidates.task_input: A synthesized gate-level netlist with scan constraints and a target fault coverage.
candidates.professional_operations: Insert scan chains, run ATPG to generate patterns, compute fault coverage, estimate defect level from yield, iterate on untestable faults.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Scan-inserted netlist, test pattern set, and fault coverage / defect level report.
candidates.success_criteria: Fault coverage meets target; defect level computed correctly; patterns are valid and compact.
candidates.verification_approach: Simulate generated patterns against the design and confirm fault detection count matches the reported coverage.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux; OpenROAD or Synopsys TestMAX (proprietary); GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: TestMAX is proprietary/licensed; OpenROAD ATPG flow is less turnkey and may need setup effort.
candidates.expert_capability: Digital design, scan methodology, ATPG and fault modeling.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: None; distinct from analog and PCB tasks.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete DFT-insert-to-coverage workflow, not a single fault simulation.

candidates.workflow_title: DC-DC power converter design and switching simulation
candidates.workflow_summary: Select topology and components for a DC-DC converter, simulate switching behavior, and verify efficiency, ripple, and stability against a specification.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.passive-components.eu/ (inductor selection for power design; search-snippet only)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Input/output voltage and current spec, efficiency target, ripple limits, available component library.
candidates.usage_permissions: Public component-selection guidance; expert provides the converter specification.
candidates.task_input: A power converter specification with input/output rails, load, efficiency and ripple targets.
candidates.professional_operations: Choose topology, size inductor/capacitors/switches, simulate switching transients and steady state, check ripple/efficiency/stability, refine component values.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Converter design with component values and a simulation report showing efficiency, ripple, and stability margins.
candidates.success_criteria: Simulated output meets voltage regulation, ripple, and efficiency targets with adequate stability margin.
candidates.verification_approach: Run an independent switching simulation (e.g., Python or a SPICE engine) and compare steady-state output, ripple, and efficiency.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Windows or Linux; SPICE (LTspice/QSPICE) or Python; GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: E3 only — the cited source was not full-text read this round; component models may be proprietary.
candidates.expert_capability: Power converter topology, magnetics, and control-loop stability.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete spec-to-verified-design workflow, not a single switch waveform.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 — confirm topology selection and stability criterion with a power electronics expert.

candidates.workflow_title: LiDAR point cloud acquisition, classification, and DEM production
candidates.workflow_summary: Take raw LiDAR point clouds through noise reduction, georeferencing, classification into ground/vegetation/building/water, and rasterized DEM/DEM production with accuracy validation.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Raw point clouds (LAS), ground-truth checkpoints, sensor calibration data, required accuracy/resolution spec.
candidates.usage_permissions: National Academies report is public; expert supplies raw LiDAR and checkpoint data with usage rights.
candidates.task_input: Raw point cloud data with an accuracy/resolution requirement and ground-truth checkpoints.
candidates.professional_operations: Run noise reduction and georeferencing, classify points, generate DEM/DTM, validate against checkpoints (RMSE per ASPRS), produce deliverables.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Classified point cloud and raster DEM with an accuracy validation report.
candidates.success_criteria: DEM meets specified RMSE against checkpoints; classification categories are correct; deliverables follow LAS/format conventions.
candidates.verification_approach: Compare DEM elevations against held-out checkpoints and check RMSE meets the stated standard.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux; PDAL/LAStools or Python (laspy/rasterio); GPU optional for large tiles.
candidates.blocking_risks: Large point clouds need storage/compute; proprietary tools (e.g., TerraScan) may be unavailable.
candidates.expert_capability: LiDAR processing, georeferencing, classification, and ASPRS accuracy standards.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: None significant; distinct from CAD/BIM and geotech tasks.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete acquisition-to-DEM life cycle, not a single filtering step.

candidates.workflow_title: Floodplain and river hydraulic modeling with HEC-RAS
candidates.workflow_summary: Build a 1D/2D river hydraulic model from geometry and flow data, run steady/unsteady simulations, and map floodplain extent and water surface elevations.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Channel/bathymetry geometry, roughness coefficients, boundary conditions, design discharge hydrographs.
candidates.usage_permissions: HEC-RAS is public US Army Corps software; expert provides geometry and flow data.
candidates.task_input: River geometry, roughness, and flow boundary conditions with a design-flood scenario.
candidates.professional_operations: Build cross-sections/terrain, assign roughness and boundary conditions, run simulation, map water surface elevation and floodplain, interpret results.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Hydraulic model with water surface profiles and a floodplain extent map.
candidates.success_criteria: Model is stable and converged; water surface elevations are physically consistent with the discharge and geometry.
candidates.verification_approach: Cross-check water surface elevation at a gauged location against the supplied rating curve or known stage.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Windows (primary) or Linux via Wine; HEC-RAS (free); GPU optional.
candidates.blocking_risks: E3 only (HEC-RAS site fetch failed this round); Windows-centric tool may complicate Linux automation.
candidates.expert_capability: Open-channel hydraulics, HEC-RAS modeling, and floodplain interpretation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: None significant; distinct from highway alignment and geotech.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete geometry-to-floodmap workflow, not a single discharge calculation.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 — confirm 1D vs 2D modeling scope with a hydraulic engineer.

candidates.workflow_title: Water distribution network hydraulic modeling with EPANET
candidates.workflow_summary: Build a pipe-network hydraulic model, assign demands and controls, run simulations, and evaluate pressure, flow, and water-quality behavior against service standards.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Network topology, pipe diameters/roughness, node demands, pump/tank characteristics, service pressure standards.
candidates.usage_permissions: EPANET is public-domain; expert supplies network and demand data.
candidates.task_input: A distribution network with demands, controls, and pressure/quality service standards.
candidates.professional_operations: Enter network and demands, assign pumps/valves/tanks and controls, run extended-period simulation, evaluate pressures/flows/quality, recommend fixes.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Calibrated hydraulic model with pressure/flow results and a service-compliance assessment.
candidates.success_criteria: All nodes meet minimum/maximum pressure standards across demand scenarios; model is mass-balanced.
candidates.verification_approach: Check mass balance and compare modeled pressures at a monitored node to supplied field data.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; EPANET (free) with Python wrapper (wntr/epanet-python).
candidates.blocking_risks: E3 only — source PDF not full-text read this round; network data availability may be limited.
candidates.expert_capability: Water distribution hydraulics, network modeling, and demand/pressure standards.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete build-simulate-assess workflow, not a single pipe headloss calc.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 — confirm demand scenarios and service standards with a water engineer.

candidates.workflow_title: Multi-storey building structural analysis and design check with ETABS
candidates.workflow_summary: Model a multi-storey building, apply gravity and lateral (seismic/wind) loads, run linear analysis, and check member forces and drifts against code limits.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Architectural/structural drawings, material grades, load data, governing design code.
candidates.usage_permissions: ETABS is proprietary (CSI); expert supplies building geometry and code parameters.
candidates.task_input: A multi-storey building with geometry, loads, and governing code provisions.
candidates.professional_operations: Build the model, assign sections/materials and loads, run analysis, check forces/drifts/foundation reactions, iterate design.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Analysis model with member force, drift, and code-check results.
candidates.success_criteria: Drifts and member demand/capacity ratios meet code limits; model is statically consistent.
candidates.verification_approach: Verify total base shear and reaction sums against hand-computed loads and confirm drift limits numerically.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Windows; ETABS/SAP2000 (proprietary) or open-source alternative; GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: E3 only — source not full-text read; ETABS license is a blocking dependency.
candidates.expert_capability: Structural analysis, seismic/wind load paths, and building code checks.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps aerospace_mech FEA conceptually but in civil building-code context.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete model-to-code-check workflow, not a single beam analysis.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 — confirm governing code and lateral-load method with a structural engineer.

candidates.workflow_title: Steady-state process simulation of a distillation column
candidates.workflow_summary: Set up a steady-state flowsheet, select thermodynamic package, run shortcut then rigorous distillation column simulation, and iterate reflux/stages to meet product specs.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Feed composition/flow, component set, thermodynamic package choice, product purity/recovery specs.
candidates.usage_permissions: Workshop summary is public; DWSIM is free/open-source; expert supplies feed and spec data.
candidates.task_input: A feed stream definition and product purity/recovery targets for a separation.
candidates.professional_operations: Add compounds, select thermodynamic package, run shortcut column (light key, min reflux, min stages), replace with rigorous column, set stages/feed/condenser-reboiler specs, add adjust controller, iterate.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Converged flowsheet with column stage/reflux design and stream mass/energy balance.
candidates.success_criteria: Products meet purity/recovery specs; mass and energy balances close; column design is physically realistic.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute overall mass balance and verify product compositions against specs with an independent check.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; DWSIM (free) or Aspen Plus/HYSYS (proprietary); GPU not required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Aspen is licensed; DWSIM lacks dynamic distillation support; thermodynamic-package selection is expertise-heavy.
candidates.expert_capability: Thermodynamics, distillation design, and steady-state simulation.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete shortcut-to-rigorous design workflow, not a single flash calc.
candidates.pending_confirmation: None — E1 source read directly; but note uncovered_official subdomain.

candidates.workflow_title: HAZOP study of a process section (node-by-node deviation analysis)
candidates.workflow_summary: Perform a structured HAZOP on a defined process section: establish design intent, divide into nodes, apply guide words to parameters, and document causes, consequences, safeguards, and recommendations.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: P&ID, process description, design intent, operating limits, existing safeguards, materials/inventory data.
candidates.usage_permissions: HAZOP book is CC-BY 4.0; expert supplies the P&ID and process information.
candidates.task_input: A process section P&ID with design intent and operating parameters.
candidates.professional_operations: Define boundaries and nodes, select parameters/guide words, develop deviations, record causes/consequences/safeguards, generate recommendations, assess safeguard independence.
candidates.expected_deliverable: HAZOP worksheet with deviations, causes, consequences, safeguards, and prioritized recommendations.
candidates.success_criteria: All meaningful deviations covered per node; recommendations are actionable; safeguard independence is considered.
candidates.verification_approach: Check coverage of guide-word/parameter combinations and validate each deviation's cause/consequence logic against the P&ID.
candidates.platform_dependencies: No specialized software required; spreadsheet/word processor; Linux or Windows.
candidates.blocking_risks: Requires a real P&ID and process data; expert judgment is the core competency and hard to automate.
candidates.expert_capability: Process safety, HAZOP facilitation, and hazard identification.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete multi-node HAZOP workflow, not a single deviation note.
candidates.pending_confirmation: None — E1 source read directly; note uncovered_official subdomain.

candidates.workflow_title: Process flow diagram and P&ID development from a process description
candidates.workflow_summary: Develop a PFD and P&ID from a textual process description, defining equipment, streams, instrumentation, and control loops consistent with the intended operation.
candidates.source_reference: No direct source read; inferred from standard process design practice (TUM process-simulation workflow only as E3 background: https://mediatum.ub.tum.de/download/1767254/1767254.pdf).
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Process description, equipment list, utility requirements, control philosophy, P&ID symbol standard.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies process description and design data; symbol standard (e.g., ISA-5.1) is public.
candidates.task_input: A process description with equipment and control requirements.
candidates.professional_operations: Translate process into a PFD, select equipment and stream connectivity, add instrumentation and control loops per ISA-5.1, produce a consistent P&ID.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A PFD and P&ID with tagged equipment, streams, and instrumentation.
candidates.success_criteria: P&ID is complete, consistent with the description, and follows symbol/tag conventions.
candidates.verification_approach: Check equipment/stream/loop completeness and consistency against the source description via a structured checklist.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; CAD or dedicated P&ID software (proprietary, e.g., AutoCAD P&ID) or open alternatives.
candidates.blocking_risks: E4 — no verified source this round; P&ID drafting tools are often proprietary; expert confirmation needed.
candidates.expert_capability: Process design, P&ID conventions (ISA-5.1), and instrumentation.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete description-to-P&ID workflow, not a single symbol placement.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E4 — requires expert confirmation of scope and symbol standard; note uncovered_official subdomain.

candidates.workflow_title: 3D scan-to-quality-decision dimensional inspection with GD&T and SPC
candidates.workflow_summary: Align a 3D scan to CAD, produce deviation maps, evaluate GD&T callouts, generate inspection reports, trend via SPC, and integrate a pass/fail decision into MES/QMS.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: 3D scan mesh/point cloud, CAD model, GD&T callouts, tolerances, SPC rules, part acceptance criteria.
candidates.usage_permissions: Vendor workflow is public; expert supplies scan data, CAD, and tolerances.
candidates.task_input: A scanned part (mesh) plus nominal CAD with GD&T and tolerances.
candidates.professional_operations: Align scan to CAD, compute color deviation map, evaluate GD&T features, write inspection report, apply SPC trending, make pass/fail decision.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Inspection report with deviation maps, GD&T results, SPC trends, and a pass/fail decision.
candidates.success_criteria: Alignment is valid; GD&T features evaluated correctly; pass/fail matches tolerance criteria.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute a subset of feature deviations from the aligned point cloud and confirm they match reported values.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; metrology software (e.g., GOM, PolyWorks — proprietary) or Python (open3d) for alignment/deviations.
candidates.blocking_risks: Metrology tools are proprietary; scan-to-CAD alignment accuracy is expertise-heavy.
candidates.expert_capability: Dimensional metrology, GD&T, and SPC interpretation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps aerospace_mech tolerance stack-up but is inspection/measurement-side rather than design-side.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete scan-to-decision workflow, not a single deviation value.

candidates.workflow_title: Statistical process control chart setup and out-of-control monitoring
candidates.workflow_summary: Collect process measurement data, establish control limits, generate X-bar/R or I-MR charts, and detect out-of-control signals for corrective action.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Process measurement data, subgroup size, control limits or historical baseline, SPC rule set (e.g., Western Electric).
candidates.usage_permissions: Public SPC guide; expert supplies measurement data and rule set.
candidates.task_input: A measurement dataset with subgrouping and an SPC rule set.
candidates.professional_operations: Compute control limits, plot control charts, apply run/trend rules, flag out-of-control points, recommend corrective action.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Control charts with limits and a list of out-of-control signals and recommendations.
candidates.success_criteria: Limits computed correctly; out-of-control signals detected per the chosen rule set.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute control limits and flag signals independently from the raw data and compare to the report.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; Python (statistical libraries) or Minitab (proprietary).
candidates.blocking_risks: Minitab is licensed; rule-set selection is expertise-heavy.
candidates.expert_capability: Statistical process control, control chart construction, and interpretation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps electronics DFT defect-level thinking only conceptually.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete data-to-monitoring workflow, not a single mean/std calculation.

candidates.workflow_title: Tolerance stack-up and process capability assessment for a machined feature
candidates.workflow_summary: Analyze manufacturing tolerance chains and process capability (Cp/Cpk) for a critical machined feature, and recommend tolerance or process adjustments.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Feature dimensions/tolerances, process measurement data, target specification limits, process capability requirements.
candidates.usage_permissions: ISO tolerancing literature is public (E3, snippet only); expert supplies dimension and process data.
candidates.task_input: A critical feature with tolerance and specification limits plus process measurement data.
candidates.professional_operations: Build tolerance chain, compute Cp/Cpk, assess capability against requirements, recommend tolerance or process changes.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Capability and stack-up report with Cp/Cpk and a recommendation.
candidates.success_criteria: Cp/Cpk computed correctly and assessed against targets; stack-up satisfies functional limits.
candidates.verification_approach: Recompute Cp/Cpk and stack-up from raw data and confirm against the report.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux or Windows; Python/spreadsheet; optionally statistical software.
candidates.blocking_risks: E3 only — source not full-text read; process data may be proprietary/unavailable.
candidates.expert_capability: Tolerance analysis, process capability, and machining process knowledge.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps aerospace_mech wf03 but is production/process-side rather than design-phase.
candidates.granularity_check: Complete stack-up-plus-capability workflow, not a single Cpk value.
candidates.pending_confirmation: E3 — confirm capability index targets and tolerance standard with a quality expert.
